scope: Source-only cross-check of the local SQL migration and regression assertions for Sol findings S59/S60.

observed: approve_onboarding rejects null and revisions below one before locks, then uses IS DISTINCT FROM for stale-revision checks before and after coordination locks.
Approval re-reads and locks the request, verifies submitted status, revalidates the privileged session, role, organization, active employee, and payload before writes.

request_onboarding_changes rejects null/invalid revisions and rechecks request status, revision, session, organization, role, and manager scope after coordination locks and while the request row is locked.

Database regressions assert invalid attempts leave status, assignments, activations, approvals, reviews, and audit rows unchanged; exact approval creates two activations once and replay preserves one review/audit record.

observed: Activity receipt replay is keyed by authenticated actor and operation ID; a reused ID with changed operation kind or arguments rejects.
A new operation ID reaches a fresh activity insert even when date, quantity, and reference match an earlier movement.
Regression assertions distinguish replay, changed-body rejection, distinct operation IDs, and legacy calls; they check distinct IDs, row count, summed quantity, audit-event count, and task revision.
